subject: Re: Redwood pricing — startup discount & committed-use options
messages:

Subject: Redwood pricing — startup discount & committed-use options

Thanks again for the call this morning — great to learn more about DeepFin's roadmap. Quick recap + next steps on pricing and discounts so we can align with procurement.

Recap from discovery:
- Pilot: ~50M tokens/month (3 month pilot window)
- Ramp: expect to reach 300–500M tokens/month within 4–6 months if pilot metrics look good
- Long-term target: 1B+ tokens/month in 12–18 months (enterprise usage across multiple products)
- Budget range for pilot: roughly $10k–$25k/month depending on model mix and latency requirements

You asked for target unit economics and how committed-use / startup discounts would affect effective $/1M tokens. Attached is a simple spreadsheet (DF_usage_estimate.xlsx) and a one-pager that outlines Redwood's committed-use tiers (Redwood-pricing-commitment-breakdown.pdf).

Key questions for us to finalize a proposal:
1) Confirm the pilot length and whether you want startup credits applied to the pilot or ramp period.
2) Confirm the monthly token bands you expect at months 3, 6, and 12 (ballpark numbers are fine).
3) Any procurement constraints on multi-year commitments (term length, auto-renew, PO vs SOW)?

High-level on discounts (summary) — we'll formalize after you confirm bands:
- Startup program: 20% off list for eligible startups (first 12 months)
- Committed-use: tiered; examples below, applied to monthly committed volume
  - 6-month commit: 10%
  - 12-month commit: 25%
  - 24-month commit: 35%
- Multi-year/incentives: additional negotiation levers (SLA credits, onboarding credits, dedicated capacity pricing) for>500M tokens/month commitments

Example (illustrative): list baseline for the model you asked about = $400 / 1M tokens.
- 12-month commit (25%) => $300 / 1M
- + Startup program (20% applied on top of committed price) => $240 / 1M effective

If that aligns, next step: I can send a simple commitment term sheet (DocuSign) with the pilot and 12-month committed tier + startup program stacked to show exact $/1M by band.

Next steps: please reply with the month-by-month volume bands you expect and whether you want us to draft a 12-month commitment term sheet (we can also prepare a 24-month scenario).

Thanks —
Marissa

Thanks Marissa — this is helpful. A couple quick clarifications before we pull procurement in:

1) Do the startup program and committed-use discounts stack? If so, are they applied sequentially (commit first, then startup) or is there a single effective percent?
2) Can you share an example P&L for 300M/mo and 500M/mo showing monthly spend at list vs committed vs committed+startup?
3) If we did a 12-month commit at 300M/mo, is there a minimum quarterly true-up schedule or is billing solely monthly per committed band?

Pilot details: we'd like the pilot to be 3 months at ~50M/mo and then re-evaluate at month 3 for ramp cadence. Budget for pilot is ~20k/mo. If committed pricing gets us to ~$240 / 1M (per your example) it's compelling for us to consider a 12-month commit after pilot.

Also looping in Aisha on procurement details.

—Samir

Great questions — answers below plus a worked example (numbers rounded) so you can share with procurement.

1) Stacking: yes — startup program is an additional credit off the committed price. We apply the committed discount to list, then apply the startup credit to the resulting committed price. That is how we get the illustrative effective price I shared.

2) Example spend (rounded) — assuming list = $400 / 1M tokens:
- 300M tokens/month:
  - list: 300 x $400 = $120,000 / month
  - 12-mo commit (25%): $120,000 * 0.75 = $90,000 / month
  - + Startup program (20% on committed price): $90,000 * 0.80 = $72,000 / month => effective $/1M = $240
- 500M tokens/month:
  - list: 500 x $400 = $200,000 / month
  - 12-mo commit (25%): $150,000 / month
  - + Startup (20%): $120,000 / month => effective $/1M = $240

3) Billing cadence / true-up: standard is monthly billing with a quarterly usage true-up for committed plans (to reconcile committed vs actual and apply overage pricing if applicable). We can discuss quarterly vs monthly true-ups if procurement requires different cadence.

4) Pilot + credit application: we can apply the startup program credits to the first 12 months starting with the pilot (i.e., pilot counts toward the 12-month period for discount eligibility). If you prefer we can start the committed term after pilot ends — just let us know which you prefer.

5) Contract terms that help with procurement: we can offer a PO-friendly SOW, SLA credits for latency/uptime, and an onboarding credit if you commit to a 24-month term. For 24-month commitments at >500M/mo we typically negotiate deeper committed rates (examples attached).

I've attached a commitment breakdown and a simple estimate (see DF_usage_estimate.xlsx). If it's useful I can send a short term-sheet via DocuSign showing the pilot + 12-month commit + startup stacking (link below).

Thanks all — quick note from procurement/ops side. Happy to take the procurement conversation and get legal looped in. A couple operational notes:

- For committed-use kitted pricing we'll propose a simple SOW that maps committed monthly bands to an annual committed volume. Quarterly true-ups are our default (can move to monthly if you prefer).
- Overages billed at the committed band list price minus the committed discount (i.e., no startup stacking on overages).
- We'll include SLA language for latency and availability if you want dedicated capacity (Ben can confirm pricing for dedicated pools).
